about: What is particular to each agent's behaviour policy: its business task where agents/JOBS.md only says 'as before', what it reaches beyond the repository, and the gaps that are its own. tools/library-abp.mjs joins this with agents/JOBS.md (the start brief), agents/policy.json (the paths), data/keys.json and CLAUDE.md to write agents/<role>/policy.md. Every line is the librarian's reading of the repository on 10 and 11 November 2026: an analysis, not agreed by Dinis, and not measured in any session but the librarian's own. The 17 entries added at 03:10 UTC on 11 November (weather to journalist) rest on each agent's line in agents/JOBS.md, its paths in agents/policy.json and its own status file only: what each agent says of itself, read by a sub-agent of the librarian's session and checked by the librarian.

measured.branches: GitHub's branches API, read 23:58 UTC on 10 November 2026: dev and main both `protected: false`
measured.session: the librarian's own session, 10 November 2026: GitHub access scoped to this one repository (push to dev works; main not tried); Claude Code Remote tools (message another session, start a session, schedule a wake); a Google Drive connector and a documents connector, both present and unused; outbound HTTPS through the environment's proxy

reach: Starts the other agents' sessions and their hourly wakes (it started the librarian's and a wake fires into it): it can start, brief and message any number of sessions.
Is the one agent in Dinis's session: what 'at Dinis's word' means reaches every other agent through it.
gap: **It holds a shared `**` rule**: it may change any path, with a warning. It integrates across folders, so the path check can never refuse it; the warnings are the only trace.
**It owns the gate, the build, the workflow and `release.sh`**: the checks that check every agent, itself included. A change that weakens a check is one commit by the agent the check binds.
It writes every agent's jobs (`agents/*/status.json`) and co-owns `agents/policy.json`: it can change what another agent is allowed or asked to do.
It commits other agents' data under its own name while their sessions cannot push here (`tools/sync-from-websummit.sh`): in the history, who wrote that data is its word.
It relays Dinis's words (BRIEF.md 'close to his words'): no other agent, and no reader, can check a quotation against the original.

reach: Its stylesheet and its part of the page frame are on every page of the site.
gap: It shares `admin/build/build.mjs` (the page frame and the front-page block): the same file holds the build, the notice 'Not a warning service' and every page's footer. The path check warns and passes.
CSS can hide, reorder or recolour what the data says (a warning level, a label) without changing a word of content; no check compares what is drawn with the data.
Screenshots of each round are to be described, not committed: the gate refuses binaries, so this one is technical.

reach: Its code under `app/agents/` runs in every reader's browser on the site's one origin, and reads GitHub's public API from there.
Pinned copies of other people's engines (Angelo's live map, Silvio's Universe) run inside its pages.
gap: **It can watch readers.** Page views are in its job ('no geo lookup' is the only limit written); what a visitor is told, and what is kept, is not yet written anywhere on this site.
It publishes what every agent is doing: a status line or an ask copied to a public page is published within a minute of the agent writing it, with no one reading it first.
Vendored engines are pinned by commit, which fixes the bytes but is not a review of them.
`admin/` pages are in its row; `admin/build/` and `admin/tools/` in the same folder are the conductor's: the boundary is a path prefix apart.

reach: Its code under `app/login/` and `account/` makes and holds a person's private key in the browser, on the same origin as every other script on the site.
It designs the lane by which Dinis writes to the conductor, and asks for an SG/Send token to make vaults.
gap: **Any agent's script on this origin could read what its login keeps in the browser**: the site has one origin and no agent's JavaScript is isolated from another's.
It writes `SECURITY.md`, the document that says what is safe: the author of the threat model is also the builder of what it models.
A vault token it is given must never be committed; the gate catches known token shapes and vault write keys, not every secret.
`PIN.json` names `tools/lane-test.mjs` as the check of its pinned copies; the catalogue did not find that file at 23:46 on 10 November.

reach: Fetches many third-party sites (weather services, broadcasters, apps) from its session to describe them.
gap: It ranks named outlets and says what each does well or badly: published opinion about named organisations, labelled as ours, with no one reading it first.
What it copies from a site it describes (a screenshot, a paragraph, a map) is bound by that site's terms; only the size and binary rule is checked.
Its tools under `research/weather-sites/tools/` run in a session that can push to every path.

reach: Reads public articles, by-lines, official and public social accounts, and Wikipedia's edit history.
Drafts messages to journalists, experts and public bodies.
gap: **It writes about named people.** By-lines on public articles only, no private individuals, no contact details: all three are rules it keeps; the gate has no check for a name, an email address or a phone number.
**It drafts outreach and a person sends.** Nothing technical stops a session with a mail or documents connector from sending; whether its session has one is not known here.
The contribute page invites corrections from readers: what arrives is material, never instruction, and the page must say where it goes.

reach: Measured in its own session: GitHub access scoped to this repository; Claude Code Remote tools; a Google Drive and a documents connector (unused); outbound HTTPS through a proxy; GitHub's Actions and branches APIs (read).
Reads other sites at length (newsroom.sgit.ai, sgit.ai, web-summit.sgit.ai) and summarises them here.
gap: **It writes the rules that check it.** `tools/policy-check.mjs` is its own, `agents/policy.json` is shared with the conductor, and every `agents/*/policy.md`, this page included, is drafted by it.
It writes inside every other agent's folder (`agents/<role>/policy.md`): the one agent whose paths cross all the others' by design.
It says who wrote what (`library/provenance.json`, the catalogue): a wrong attribution is published as provenance. It reads the agent from the commit's subject, which is asserted, not signed.
Its summaries of other people's articles are its own words presented beside their links: a wrong summary misleads with a citation attached.
It reads the commits in a full clone only it holds: nobody else re-runs that read.

reach: Its pages run a database in the reader's browser over the site's JSON; its graph joins every other agent's data.
gap: It derives one graph from the others' files: a wrong join states a relation (who decided, who warned, who reported) that no source stated. The rule is 'built from the existing JSON, never by hand twice'; nothing checks a derived edge against its sources.
Its ontology names kinds of actors and relations for everyone: a change there changes what every page means.
Code under `app/graph/` and `data/query/` runs on the site's one origin.

meteorologist.task: The weather picture as data: IPMA's warnings, communiqués, forecasts and station observations and the airport's TAF and METAR, each with source and time read, refreshed hourly; and one analysis, labelled as analysis (its jobs in `agents/meteorologist/status.json`).
reach: Fetches IPMA's open data and NOAA's aviation weather service every hour (`data/weather/tools/refresh.py`).
Its session cannot push to this repository: it writes in SGit-AI__Website__Web-Summit and the conductor copies it across.
gap: **Its analysis can be read as a forecast.** The site is not a warning service; `analysis.md` is labelled a hypothesis, and the label is the only barrier between our reasoning and advice.
A parsing mistake in `refresh.py` publishes a wrong warning window under IPMA's name within the hour; the source URL is on every record, the bytes read are not kept (no raw vault).
Its data reaches this repository in the conductor's commits: in the history here, the meteorologist never committed.

researcher.task: The decision graph (who decides what, when, following what) and the list of every source with its status, reuse terms and how it can be read (its jobs in `agents/researcher/status.json`).
reach: Reads official, press and organiser pages and public social posts.
Its session cannot push to this repository: it writes in SGit-AI__Website__Web-Summit and the conductor copies it across.
gap: It labels what is fact, evidence or hypothesis about named bodies: a wrong label states a report as a decision.
It decides what may be reused (`reuse`, `reuse_basis` in `sources.json`): a licence judgement nobody else reviews.
Where a site refuses machines (a bot check), the rule is that a person reads it; nothing technical stops a session from trying.
Its data reaches this repository in the conductor's commits.

dev.task: The connectors and the dashboard: the Web Summit watch (`tools/websummit*`), the timeline converter, the model ledger's wrapper (`tools/llm.mjs`) and `app/storm.js` (its jobs in `agents/dev/status.json`).
reach: Polls third-party sites on a short cycle (every 2 minutes for the organiser's blog).
Its wrapper is the one path to third-party models (OpenRouter) and to the spend.
Its session cannot push to this repository yet; the conductor copies its work across.
gap: **Model calls and money.** Every call is to go through `tools/llm.mjs` (a rule); the daily cap is inside the wrapper (technical, in a file an agent can edit). A call made around the wrapper is uncounted.
A poller is code run on a loop in a session that can push: a review found the first version ran unreviewed code within 2 minutes; the pinned copy fixed it, as a design choice, not a platform limit.
`app/storm.js` runs on the site's one origin and draws the decision: a mistake there shows a wrong status to every reader.
It reads robots.txt and obeys it (its own code): a rule it implements, not one imposed on it.

reach: Its pages under `studio/` and `app/studio/` run animations in the reader's browser, on the site's one origin.
gap: **It explains with invented characters and simplified pictures.** An explanation is our analysis: a simplification that reads as a fact about how an assistant or this team works is a hypothesis shown as fact, on a site whose rule is that the two never look alike.

It takes its look from other sites and a book (storyboard.sgit.ai, The Ultimate Insider): what it copies is bound by their terms; images are binaries the gate refuses, drawings in code are not checked.
Code under `app/studio/` runs beside the login's keys in the browser, as every agent's script does.

reach: Reads Wikipedia's articles and their revision histories in every language through the MediaWiki API, on a schedule (`tools/wikipedia-*.mjs`).
gap: **It reads editors.** A revision history names the accounts and IP addresses that edited: public, and still data about people. The rule is no profiles of private people; a dataset of revisions keyed by editor is one step from a profile, and nothing checks what columns it keeps.

**It could edit Wikipedia.** Its mandate is to read and compare; an agent that finds an error there may be tempted to fix it. Editing is a message outside the repositories: agents draft, a person sends, and nothing technical stands in the way.
It judges this site and Wikipedia against Wikipedia's values (verifiability, neutrality, no original research): our analysis, published with no second reader, about a named project.
Wikipedia's text is CC BY-SA: what it copies in full carries a share-alike licence into a repository whose data is Apache-2.0; only size and binaries are checked.

reach: Its script under `app/weather/` runs in every reader's browser at `/`, the front door of the site.
Its status says it reads only the data room's published JSON (`api/v1/2026-11-10-storm-charles/` and `incident.json`) and fetches nothing external.
The conductor's scheduled checks wake it (05:25 and 09:25 UTC on 11 November).
gap: **It is the first screen a reader sees, and it must request no outside address.** The gate refuses a release whose Weather face code names one (`admin/build/validate.mjs`, since 02:32 UTC on 11 November); an address built at run time would pass that check.

It composes one sentence from IPMA's warnings and draws the meteorologist's reading as a dashed hypothesis: the rule that this is not a warning service rests on that wording and that line style staying apart.
It already removed one heading of its own that was a claim with no source ('where the storm arrived first'); nothing but its own review caught it.
It shows IPMA's sentence in English, sometimes in the meteorologist's translation; its own ask notes that the English for orange and red rain reads alike while the Portuguese differs.

reach: Reads IPMA's open data (the documented addresses at api.ipma.pt and IPMA's own directory listings) about hourly with `tools/ipma-read.mjs`, one request every 3 seconds, read-only.
Keeps the reads in a data vault; the read key is published in `sources/ipma/dataset.json`.
Asks Dinis to send the email IPMA requests of users of its API; an agent does not send email.
gap: **Its vault key was sent to the conductor in the clear by session message** and its status says to treat it as known to anyone who can read the two transcripts: the exposure is write access to copies of public data.
IPMA's terms ask users to say by email that they use the service, ask for its logo beside its data, and are silent on reshaping the data: all three wait on Dinis while the hourly reads go on.
It records IPMA's licence as 'not stated' and labels everything it computes as ours; every page that draws IPMA's numbers depends on that reading.
It has found addresses outside the documented open data with no stated terms; whether to read them is an open ask, and one other agent already reads one such file.

reach: Reads MeteoAlarm's Portugal feed on each hourly round with `tools/source-meteoalarm.mjs`, and reads the licence and terms pages of the bodies it registers.
Keeps the full feed copies in a data vault whose key is held only in its own session; git keeps a pointer and each file's sha256 in `sources/meteoalarm/dataset.json`.
Has asked Dinis whether to get a key for MeteoAlarm's archive, which would be an account in a person's name.
gap: **The key of its vault exists only in its session.** Its permission check refused both ways of handing it over and it did not work around them, so no read key is published and nobody else can write there.
The licence status of each of 46 bodies in `sources/sources.json` is its reading; other pages rely on it when they quote or draw a source.
It keeps the list of sites that forbid automated reading (link only, no requests); that promise is kept by its own tools, and analysis: no gate check for it was found in the files read.
The open feed drops replaced messages, so its record has holes it cannot fill without the archive key (Madeira's Tuesday-afternoon warnings are in no read).

reach: `tools/capture.mjs` opens every outside address the timeline and decisions cite, one at a time, under a plain client name, obeying robots.txt and never logged in; primary sources are re-read each hour.
Keeps two vaults: a display vault whose read key is published in `data/vaults.json`, and a packed capture vault whose read key is not published.
Its page under `app/evidence/` reads the screenshot from the display vault in the reader's browser.
gap: **The write keys of both vaults are held only in its session.** The permission check refused reading them back, so they were never sent; until Dinis decides the route nobody else can write to either vault.
The capture vault holds raw press pages that must stay private; which captures are shown and which are kept privately is its decision alone (for example six of ten studies shown, four kept).
A faulty pattern of its own cut addresses short and 23 captures were of pages nobody cites; ten had been released before it noticed, and their records remain in git history.
Sites that answer 403, have an unreadable robots.txt or disallow all are recorded as not captured, so the evidence is thinner for those sources than a reader may assume.

reach: Its status records no outside reads: the nodes are made from `entities/seed.json` (hand-kept) and the site's own rows, decisions and files.
Its linker runs as the build's 'after' step over every built page, and `app/lens/lens.js` runs in the reader's browser inside the designer's panel.
The linker sends an outside link to its evidence page when the archivist has a capture of it.
gap: **It changes other agents' pages after they are built**: about 28,000 mentions are linked on each build, so one wrong name match puts a wrong link on pages their owners never see.
Which things are nodes is decided by hand in `entities/seed.json`; public roles are kept as roles, and the rule against profiles of private people depends on that file staying so.
Redirecting an outside link to our capture changes where a reader lands; the page must still show the source's own address.
Its build lists names with no node yet (83 at the last count), so the linked view is partial and can look complete.

reach: `app/labs/labs.js` runs in the reader's browser and, by its status, loads only the site's published JSON.
It reads other agents' data (the graph's tables, the media first-on-each-fact file, the meteorologist's weather files) and nothing outside the site is recorded in its status.
One experiment (day-bands) was lifted onto the front page by `incident.weather@`.
gap: **Its pages are experiments published live.** Each says what it shows badly, but a reader arriving by link may take a trial view for the record.
The models view draws four model runs against what was measured, labelled 'never our forecast': the rule against forecasts of our own depends on that label holding on every view.
Some views rebuild the past (IPMA's warnings at any minute from the kept messages; Tuesday from what the files still hold); a rebuilt mark must never look like one read from the feed.
The lag view measures when a warning was read into our data against when it was sent; its own note says the long bars do not all measure what they seem to.

reach: Reads every agent's status file, the timeline, `decisions.md` and the decision graph on each wake; it answered one card from Web Summit's own public page.
`app/board/board.js` runs in the reader's browser, also embedded on the agents' pages and on Contribute.
Publishes tasks for outside contributors in `board/tasks.json`.
gap: **It turns each agent's asks into cards and could drop, merge or reword one.** The same ask from several agents becomes one card, and some cards for Dinis were written by hand from several agents' lines.
It owns the one list of what Dinis can unblock and ranks it; what he sees first is its ordering.
An ask whose line has gone is listed to be read by hand, never closed by the tool: closing depends on the agent doing that reading each wake.
Its own tool refuses an address or a personal link on a card; that check is written and run by the agent it checks.

reach: Reads Bluesky's public API with no account, 3 seconds between requests (`tools/social-read.mjs`); no account was made.
Hands the archivist a list of official posts to capture and offers the conductor things the timeline lacks.
Plans to read Mastodon's official accounts, and X only where readable without logging in.
gap: **It decides which accounts count.** `research/social/accounts.json` lists 18 accounts of organisations and public roles with why each counts; a private person must never be on that list or in a kept post.

It counts the public conversation per hour and per language and says nothing of a private person is written to disk; that is kept by its own tool, and analysis: no gate check for a name or handle was found in the files read.
Its offers become timeline rows when the conductor takes them (three so far), so a misread post could reach the record.
'Who did not post' is stated from where it looked and found no account; an account it missed would make that line wrong.

reach: `tools/meteorology-read.mjs` fetches the page each edge and each licence cites and stamps state, time, sha256 and a quote; every edge is re-read each three hours.
Probed ten open weather sources for Lisbon and Madeira and keeps four small samples; no model field is in git.
Two of its proposals need a person: registering with EUMETSAT and accepting its licence, and a decoder run outside the build.
gap: **Its licence table is what others build on.** `meteorology/licences.json` gives four answers per source (read, store, show, transform); they are its reading of each page, and several are still 'unclear'.
Its six-model table puts model output beside IPMA's warnings; it is labelled evidence with no average and no pick, and the rule against forecasts of our own depends on that staying so.
Of 226 edges, 54 are 'not stated' on the page cited and 22 were not read; the map draws them all, so a reader must be able to tell them apart.
It found that some satellite imagery newer than one hour may not be shown publicly; a build-on item taken up without that condition would break a licence.

reach: Builds only from the data room: timeline rows, data fields with the value they held when written, and decision edges; nothing outside the site is recorded in its status.
`app/stories/` runs in the reader's browser with switches for sources, times and the hypothesis layer; IPMA's red warnings for Lisbon are read again there.
A scheduled re-check wakes its session each hour after the data read.
gap: **It states conclusions.** Each story mixes facts, evidence and hypotheses (26 claims in the first, four of them hypotheses) under one title, and a reader may carry away the hypothesis as the finding.
A sentence is written on a value at one time; if the field moves, the build flags it beside the sentence, but the retelling waits for the agent's next wake.
Its `--check` proves that every support resolves, not that the sentence says what the support says: that reading is the agent's alone.
Its own list of what it could not support (whether lead times were enough, why two official positions differ) marks where a story could slide into judgement.

reach: Calls other models through a provider with `tools/llm.mjs`, using a key from the environment; 13 models were measured in round 1.
Keeps every request and response in an encrypted vault outside git; the vault key is held only in its session.
Offers `tools/models-ask.mjs` as the one call other desks use.
gap: **It owns `tools/llm.mjs`, the single door for every model call**, and `agents/policy.json` lists that file under `incident.dev@` as well: two owners for the tool the model rule depends on.
The team's daily cap is kept as per-agent shares because a ledger lives in each session; no shared counter exists, so the total is known only when each desk reports its own summary.
Gold answers are copied from the data room and scored by its own tool; `models/which.json` then tells other agents which model to use for which job.
The raw store's key cannot be read out of its session, so nobody else can open the requests and responses behind its scores.

reach: Asks answer engines with web search a fixed set of questions through `tools/llm.mjs`; the full answers are kept only outside git.
Lists every address an engine pointed a reader at in `shadow/cited.json` as candidates for capture, and read one news API's terms at source without signing up for any.
Its tool maps one environment key name to another in its own process, because the name `tools/llm.mjs` reads differs from the one the environment sets.
gap: **It relays what answer engines say.** It restates each answer as statements in our words and labels them itself against the timeline and the graph (match, behind, ahead, contradict, unsupported).
Statements 'ahead of us' are published as leads; a lead is not a fact until someone reads it at the source, and the page must keep the two apart.
The cited addresses were chosen by an engine, not read by us; listing them can look like sourcing.
When the provider's account has no credit the hourly table has gaps, so the comparison over time is uneven.

reach: `tools/ci-read.mjs` reads GitHub's Actions API and a full clone of the repository into `data/ci/`, outside the build's hot path.
Writes `ci/patches/` for the conductor to apply to the release script and the gate, and a tool that signs and verifies a release record with an agent's own key.
Reports queues, failures and the gate's time to the conductor at each wake.
gap: **It proposes patches to the gate it reports on**: the conductor applies them, but the same agent measures the pipeline and designs changes to it.
`README.md` is listed under both the conductor and this agent in `agents/policy.json`: a stranger's first page has two owners.
Its pages say what is and is not signed; a signed release record waits on Dinis's yes, so until then 'who pushed' rests on commit subjects and trailers.
Times it first wrote were estimates up to ten minutes ahead of the clock, corrected by itself; its status gives the gate's budget as 5 seconds where `CLAUDE.md` says 8.

reach: Asks Perplexity's engine open questions in Portuguese and English through `tools/llm.mjs`; the full text stays outside git.
`tools/perplexity-check.mjs` opens the cited addresses one at a time and, by its status, never the forbidden or social hosts.
Retries one call every half hour while the provider's account has no credit.
gap: **It relays an answer engine's findings as leads**, and the conductor has already taken two into a timeline row; each must be read at the body's own address first, which this desk says it does.
Of 19 statements in round 1, 7 were confirmed at a primary source, 8 were press only and 4 unsupported: the scorecard is its own judgement of its own tool's answers.
The list of hosts it must never open is kept in its own tool; analysis: no file read here shows another check of it.
Its spend is known to the team only through the ledger summary it writes itself.

reach: Reads the model ledger's summary, `incident.ci@`'s run data, the provider account's state (`accounts/provider.json`) and the ledger lines each session writes.
Asks every agent to run its measure step at the end of each wake, and used two sub-agents to measure the librarian's pack.
Writes a brief for Dinis each round in `accounts/briefs/`.
gap: **Its numbers depend on each agent measuring itself.** At round 3 four sessions were in the ledger and nine more had reported by message; a session that does not run the step is simply missing.
Other agents now push their own lines into `accounts/ledger/`, a folder it owns: what it totals is written by those it counts.
`accounts/savings.md` says where to cut; analysis: a saving drawn from partial figures could steer the team wrongly.
Its books record sessions (who started each, when); nothing from a key store and nothing about where anyone is may enter them.

reach: Its status records no outside reads: traces are made from commits, the brief, and the files other agents keep.
Reads whole commit messages, because some `For:` trailers are invisible to git's trailer parser.
Feeds `incident.journalist@` and the briefing pack through `reporter/traces/`.
gap: **It writes the record of who said what and when.** Of 82 steps in six traces, three are marked 'no evidence', and the journal is told from these traces.
The brief's times for Dinis's words run a few minutes later than the commits that record them; which the record follows is an open ask, so its times are approximate.
`reporter/numbers.json` counts by hour from files other agents keep; a wrong file upstream becomes a wrong number here with no second check.
Analysis: a trace of the team's work must never carry where anyone is or anything said in private; that rests on the agent alone.

reach: Its status records no outside reads: pieces are told from the reporter's traces, `data/ci/`, the brief, the board's cards and data fields.
`app/journal/` runs a small script in the reader's browser that places each picture under its heading.
Builds `journal/edition.md` as a print article at build time (never committed), from which a PDF is to be made.
gap: **It tells the story of the project in prose**, and its three pieces are live as drafts while their supports are still being traced.
Its first piece said 77 cards waited on Dinis where the board's figure was 36 (a pattern of its own matched too much); it corrected the page with a dated note.
Its build resolves every support, yet three statements are 'not recorded' and the times of Dinis's directions are the brief's approximations.
Its pictures and counts stop at the last read of `data/ci/`; a reader may take them as current.
